note: No .env or env example is in the repo and no file was blocked. All Gemini calls are server side (google-genai in src/agents/base.py), so there are no ai_browser_call or secret_exposure labels. Storage is JSON checkpoints in a GCS bucket keyed by a random 128-bit session token. There are no user accounts and no database, so no database_rules labels. The app has no tool that sends, pays or books anything. Real protections: user-driven stage advance behind deterministic gates, allergy null-gating, project-type backstop, fenced untrusted contractor quote, internal-code scrub, per-session chat rate limit, live extraction that refuses to fabricate on failure. Of the src/tools calculators, only pricing_ballpark and allergy_screen are called at runtime. Lighting_calc, envelope_check and measurement_math are dead code. The prompts in .agents and .specify say the matching numbers come from those tools. | Second labeler: Gemini is called only from the server, so there is no ai_browser_call. No .env is committed and no key is in client code, so no secret_exposure. Storage is a GCS bucket with no client access, so no database_rules. The app is anonymous by design, using a session token, so no auth_gap. No tool moves money or sends anything, so there is no ai_tool_unbounded. The main risk is safety logic that the prompts call code-validated (tiers, envelopes, material math), which the model does. The deterministic tools for these exist but are never called. A silent switch to mock mode fabricates plans. Not reviewed: research/, tests/, evidence-deliverables/ (committed sample PDF and xlsx files), the other skills and workflows beyond grep, and index.css. No file was blocked.

labels.what: If the Gemini client fails to build (bad credentials, missing project), the agent sets MOCK_VERTEX_AI=true for the whole process. Every stage then returns canned text such as Materials line items compiled. No allergy conflicts found (lines 671-692), shown to the homeowner as a real answer

Mock extraction fills the dossier with invented values: zip 95120, 80 sq ft, allergies confirmed none, a Mock electrical wiring safety item with consent already true, materials marked allergy-screened, quote coverage marked present, design estimates of 19000-22000. It runs whenever mock mode is on, including the silent fallback, so gates pass on made-up consent and the plan PDF is built from it

Constitution says Materials runs a code-level numeric check of each product against the stored safety envelope and reopens Safety on a breach. validate_envelope is never called. The envelope_check value on each line item comes from LLM extraction and orchestrator.py line 206 trusts it

Constitution says measurement math, quantity and waste, cost-band lookup and unit-match run as deterministic tools. Only the scope ballpark and the allergy screen are coded. Room area, design refined estimates, over_ceiling and gap_amount, and material extended_cost are LLM-extracted and merged as-is. The Materials agent also has live web search on (src/agents/materials.py line 28)
Prompt says fixture-count and lumen math is a deterministic tool. calculate_lighting_requirements is never called. Lighting numbers come from the model

The Tier-1 thresholds (structural, panel electrical, gas, framed floor at 1500 lb filled) live only in the prompt. The Safety gate (orchestrator.py 397-404) checks only that source and rationale strings exist. DIY eligibility (orchestrator.py 48) uses whatever tier the model wrote, so a misclassified Tier-1 item gets a DIY procedure
Prompt says permit_required is true when any item is Tier-2 or higher. Code never derives it. The gate trusts the LLM-extracted flag, so permit consent is skipped if the model leaves it false

The Tier-1 firewall (never give DIY procedure for professional-only work) is a prompt rule in chat. run_chat returns the model text after scrubbing only internal codes. Nothing checks the reply for Tier-1 how-to steps

Rule says allergies must be screened against material choices. The code only matches whole word tokens of material, category and brand names against the allergy list, so an allergen not named in the product title passes as screened

Prompt says a Tier-2 DIY procedure MUST include the permit and inspection hold points. The DIY gate (orchestrator.py 489-498) never checks hold_points, so a permitted-work procedure with no permit step passes into the plan
Prompt says implausible measurements are flagged and never fed into area math. validate_room_dimensions exists but is never called, and room area comes from LLM extraction

Prompt says ask for the budget ceiling when only one number is given. Code copies the target into the ceiling when it is missing (base.py 1525-1528), so the scope gate's ceiling check passes without the family stating one
Prompt lists what a complete quote MUST itemize. The contractor gate only checks that coverage_check is non-empty, so one audited line passes and missing rubric items are never detected by code
Prompt limits each reply to 3 questions. Nothing in code counts questions in the reply

Tier-1 acknowledgement is a regex over every past user turn. Phrases like I don't want to hire a contractor match, and Tier-1 items added later are auto-marked acknowledged, so the family's consent step can be recorded without them giving it

The paid Gemini chat is rate limited per session cookie only. /api/session/new has no limit, so a script mints new sessions and gets a fresh bucket each time. Each chat turn makes two or more model calls

Every chat logs the full dossier (allergies, health sensitivities, occupant ages, budget, zip) plus the session token at DEBUG, and the logging config writes DEBUG to a file. Session tokens are also logged on most routes

The session token is kept in localStorage (lines 32, 138, 351) and every endpoint accepts it from the JSON body, so the HttpOnly cookie gives no protection. The token is the only key to the family's dossier

Untrusted PDF restore says it resets to Scope for re-walk, but reopen_stage_and_cascade keeps the imported user_final_verdict on scope and never resets the design stage (not in stages_init). The next chat turn can pass both gates on values from the uploaded file. Upload size is also unbounded (line 1060)
Error handlers return str(exc) in details to the browser (also lines 963 and 1076), leaking internal error text such as GCS and model errors
appendSystemMessage and appendSystemWarning write text with innerHTML, including the uploaded file name (line 340) and server error detail. Agent text uses textContent
The full dossier JSON, including allergies, health sensitivities and occupant ages, is embedded in the blueprint PDF that families are told to share with contractors

Any GCS write error silently falls back to JSON files in the shared temp directory with default permissions. With more than one instance the session is then lost, and read_session does the same fallback
Cost bands are hardcoded and the regional multiplier table has one entry, ZIP 95120 (San Jose, the demo zip). Every other ZIP is priced at the national 1.0x baseline with no warning to the family
Rate limit text says 1 chat request per minute (also middleware line 75 and app.js line 176), but the config allows 10 per minute with a burst of 5
GCS bucket name defaults to reno-compass-checkpoints, a global bucket name that may belong to someone else
Budget-gap bridge options and every phase checklist are the same fixed strings for every project. The plan PDF presents them as the family's own plan
Regional cost table has one demo ZIP (95120 = 1.55x). Every other ZIP silently gets 1.0, while the app promises cost for the user's ZIP code.
Allergy 'screen' only checks whether an allergen word appears in the product's own name, category or brand. It has no ingredient data, so most real conflicts are stamped allergy_screened=True.

Mock replies tell the user 'No allergy conflicts found', 'Safety permit classifications logged' and 'Task completed successfully' with no model call or check run. They reach real users after the silent fallback.
When the GCS write fails, the session is saved to the container's temp folder and the request still succeeds. On restart or another instance the session is gone.
Default scope object starts with allergies=[] (means family confirmed none), budget check 'plausible', a house and owner-occupied. If extraction is skipped or fails, these stand as real answers.
Directive says a Tier-2 DIY procedure MUST include permit and inspection hold-points. The merge accepts an empty hold_points list and the DIY gate never checks it.

Prompt says an allowance unit mismatch makes the tool refuse to compute, and allergy handling is code-validated. No unit-match or extended-cost code exists. Quantities, waste and totals are model numbers copied into the xlsx.

Design prompt lists measurement math, IES lighting calc and a refined-estimate cost tool. None is called. Room area, lighting and over_ceiling come from the model, and synthesis uses over_ceiling to decide the budget gap. The 40 ft implausible-size check never runs.
Tier-1 acknowledgement is recorded on every Tier-1 item when any user turn matches a loose regex ('understood', 'hire a contractor'), even if said about something else.
Session token is only checked for the 'reno_s_' prefix, then joined into a file path in local-fallback mode, so '../' can reach JSON files outside the session folder.
Service-account JSON from an env var is written to a temp file with delete=False and never removed.
The raw user message goes into the model prompt next to the trusted dossier state with no guard. The Tier-1 firewall depends on the prompt resisting pressure.
